newsitem.title: USA: Digital Descriptor appeals NASDAQ delisting move.
newsitem.headline: Digital Descriptor appeals NASDAQ delisting move.

text.p: Digital Descriptor Systems Inc, a developer and marketer of computer installations, said Thursday it has began an appeals process on a move by Nasdaq to delist its stock effective May 23.

Garrett Cohen, president of the company, said in a statement that Digital Descriptor was deemed not to meet the $2 million total asset and $1 million capital surplus requirements, "although total assets at December 31, 1996 were $1,929,808 and capital and surplus $1,108,536."
He said Nasdaq excluded from assets a $150,000 certificate of deposit pledged for a bank loan. But the loan has been reduced to $82,000, he said.
He said Digital Descriptor is in talks with several lenders for additional funding.
"We will make every effort to meet Nasdaq requirements for listing," he said.

He said the company's gross margins were increasing and sales were running at record levels. In addition, operating losses have been sharply reduced and expenses for 1997 projected at $2.8 million against $4.1 million for 1996, he said.
With these developments, he said "we believe the company has realistic expectations of again meeting Nasdaq requirements."
